1422665730416328704 [2021-08-03] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 63 🔁 4
Your subconscious drives are reorganizing your mind to try new strategies til one works, and since they aren't conscious, they aren't constrained by:
• what you think is okay
• your own… belief… that you're not allowed to fuck around and find out?!? 🤯
↓
1422665732379267083 [2021-08-03] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 18
Holy shit that actually explains why your subconscious seems (/is?) smarter than you!

This came from @jondubin pointing at the question of why a given part wins an internal conflict. Not sure I'd seriously thought about it like that before.
↓
1422665744224034832 [2021-08-03] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 12
From a PCT lens, when there's a direct internal conflict, nobody wins, it's just a tug of war that either stabilizes at some compromise (with both sides still tugging full-force!) or oscillates if perturbed from that compromise. https://t.co/XFRq3VCTjp
Images:
  - [Image #0] The image depicts a cartoon man engaged in a tug-of-war with an unseen force on a beach. The man, with dark hair and a mustache, is shirtless and wearing sunglasses, pulling on a rope that appears to be coming from the sea. 
    
    To the right of the image, three individuals are standing on a bench, watching the scene unfold. The background features a serene blue sky with a single white cloud, a calm sea, and a sandy beach.
↓
1422665746203783168 [2021-08-03] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 12
But what if the internal conflict is indirect?

Brain is a learning system and in general tries to reorganize itself in order to achieve the various aims it's pursuing at various levels.

And I've long been aware eg school traumatizes ppl away from that natural learning process…
↓
1422665747847860228 [2021-08-03] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 12
…but I'm realizing that there might be a sense in which the learning process itself goes underground a bit, and renders shadow parts more capable of outwitting you than you are at outwitting them!

Hence the experience of these persistent weird desires that can't be tamed.
↓
1422665749512998912 [2021-08-03] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 15 🔁 1
The brain's learning/reorganization system is kind of endlessly creative as long as it's able to run. But when we're doing things consciously we often think we know how they should work and we don't let the reorganization happen naturally. Or if the first try fails, we give up.
↓
1422665751211778048 [2021-08-03] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 11
By contrast, if our unconscious drives are, by their nature, not under conscious control and thus also can't be criticized into giving up (to avoid fear of failure)…

…they'll just keep trying stuff, and sooner or later come up with a new way to thwart most counteractive moves!
↓
1422665752914665473 [2021-08-03] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 7
The takeaway here is that just because your shadow parts manage to win a bunch of your internal conflicts, doesn't mean that those desires are more true for you.

Conflict is a whole phenomenon itself!
https://t.co/6lpoE7yIo2
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: "having is evidence of wanting" — @carolynelliott_  This is true, on net, but can easily form an Over-reified Revealed Preferences frame, in that it doesn't account for the emergent results of conflict!  ...which is what's underneath most behavior, particularly confusing behavior]
↓
1422665762053967872 [2021-08-03] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 15
No, I spoke too soon. The *real* takeaway here is that you can't beat your shadow in a fight. https://t.co/zDaMyO9CMr

1523746020831551488 [2022-05-09] @visakanv 💜 109 🔁 3
when I was a kid I was subjected to vague comforting ideas like “people in charge must be smart” and that “people must listen to wise people” – and “must” here is doing a lot of work bc it can mean so many things, and most people don’t even know what they mean when they say it
↓
1523746569329070081 [2022-05-09] @visakanv 💜 46
reality is so much sillier than this. a wise person can be embedded in a community, be visibly happier, more well-adjusted, at peace, etc, and yet her peers will often not really see this about her, and those that do will often ignore it, and some will even get mad about it
↓
1523746909952745473 [2022-05-09] @visakanv 💜 23
I actually never found much comfort in the vaguely comforting ideas, of which I’m sure you can think of a bunch too - “everything happens for a reason”, “what goes around comes around,” etc. yes, after 20 years of study and reflection etc I can make those statements work for me,
↓
1523747798344101888 [2022-05-09] @visakanv 💜 33 🔁 1
but in practice they’re often used as placeholders. *substitutes* for thought. if we use them as *starting* points for inquiry, that’s alright in my book, but if we use them dismissively, to discourage closer examination, that worries me, because that is a setup for disaster
↓
1523748985059430400 [2022-05-09] @visakanv 💜 19
people learn very slowly, which can be quite an exercise in patience to witness

(not all learning is slow; only learning that is inhibited by poor conditions, internal blockages, emotional disturbances, etc)
↓
1523749157004922882 [2022-05-09] @visakanv 💜 28
the nature of constraints is such that we’re left with our worst and most wicked problems bc we solve the rest. we avoid the pits we can avoid, we climb out of the pits we can climb out of, and we end up mostly stuck in the pits we could neither avoid nor climb out of
↓
1523749512929443840 [2022-05-09] @visakanv 💜 22 🔁 1 [(SEED) type=quote_of_root]
and even that metaphor is a little too on the nose because in practice the pits don’t look or feel like pits and we don’t even realize we’re in them when we’re in them https://t.co/gRt9PdXNI8

1643493974370398210 [2023-04-05] @RichDecibels 💜 70 🔁 1
here is a roundabout story to show how I understand adult development

on Saturday I narrowly avoided a severe traffic accident, I got within an inch of totalling someone's car and probably maiming or killing them
↓
1643494678715670532 [2023-04-05] @RichDecibels 💜 21
I had entered an uncontrolled intersection, cutting across 3 lanes of crossing traffic. the van I'm driving has a massive blindspot due to the front left pillar and the awkward drivers seat position. so I couldn't see the small Fiat barrelling towards us at speed
↓
1643495165192024065 [2023-04-05] @RichDecibels 💜 24
but my wife Nati is in the passenger seat, she can see the Fiat clearly, so she warned me to get out of the way. I had no awareness of the threat, but I trust that she only freaks out when necessary, and I know she can see things I can't, so I stomped the brakes and swerved
↓
1643495655636180992 [2023-04-05] @RichDecibels 💜 32
we were a split second away from a grisly ending, but her perspective and our relationship prevented disaster

OK so what does this say about adult development?
↓
1643496607122423808 [2023-04-05] @RichDecibels 💜 48 🔁 1
my development is obscured by blindspots. I have habits and unconscious commitments that keep me locked into self defeating patterns. the blindspot obscures threats as well as it obscures the next step in my growth journey. I can't see my way out of this conundrum from my POV
↓
1643497119716634625 [2023-04-05] @RichDecibels 💜 51
I need a second perspective, someone who knows where I'm sitting, knows what I can't see. I need to know where they're sitting, to trust they'll know things I can't know

I need to trust their intentions, if they say RICH GO NOW, I need to commit to the action without hesitation
↓
1643498449923371009 [2023-04-05] @RichDecibels 💜 45
there are moments in the developmental journey where I need to step off a cliff blindfolded, knowing my companion can see a safe footing that's invisible to me. I need to override the inner signals telling me I'm approaching mortal danger, and trust their guidance  ☠️
↓
1643502160221462528 [2023-04-05] @RichDecibels 💜 52 🔁 1
if you don't have the right companions right now, you can kinda simulate a second perspective with practices like journalling, insight meditation, psychedelics, theatre etc

but just be aware if you go alone you're going the long way round
↓
